reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must refuse a PAGE clause whose FOOTING integer-5 is less than its LAST DETAIL integer-4, in either phrase order (SR1), where an omitted phrase takes its GR2 implicit value (LAST DETAIL omitted: integer-4 = integer-5; FOOTING omitted: integer-5 = integer-4; both omitted: both = integer-1), so only a pair written with FOOTING < LAST DETAIL can violate it.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.DialectLevel < 2002: the three-significant-digit bound of integer-1 (SR2), not this rule
ConstructRegistry ReportPageForms2002: refuses LAST CONTROL HEADING / DE / IS at 85, so the 1985 order set is HEADING, FIRST DETAIL, LAST DETAIL, FOOTING, page limit

reader.edition-search: The ordering loop in ScreenReportPageIntegers itself consults no edition (one arm for every edition); the edition sites on the path are the SR2 digit bound and the VersionConformancePass refusal of the 2002 phrases.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the ascending-order comparison of LAST DETAIL to FOOTING is the same code at 85 and 2023; 2023 adds LAST CONTROL HEADING to the chain, which 85 refuses (COBOL0900)

reader.notes: ScreenReportPageIntegers sorts the WRITTEN phrases into PagePhrase order and compares each to the next written one (then the page limit), so LAST DETAIL vs FOOTING is checked whenever both are written and the GR2 defaults can never violate SR6. The diagnostic cites only §2023:13.18.39.3 SR6 at --std 85, a citation-only blemish, not a verdict defect.

refuter.evidence: Read ReportSectionBinder.cs#ScreenReportPageIntegers: written phrases sorted into PagePhrase order and each compared with the next written one, so LAST DETAIL vs FOOTING is compared whenever both are written; GR2 d/e defaults copy one into the other and cannot violate SR6.
